events.title: 'Trump Needs a Way Out of This War': General Yakovlev explains 'charade' over US-Iran negotiations
events.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome General Michel Yakovleff, Professor at Sciences-Po and Former Vice-Chief of Staff at NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (Shape).. He presents a strategic rather than tactical reading of the current lull in the US-Iran conflict. He argues that the apparent de-escalation is not evidence of diplomatic progress but of mounting structural constraints. Rather than viewing pauses in hostilities as signs of imminent peace, he frames them as consequences of political pressure, military logistics and industrial limitations. At the centre of his argument is the proposition that modern warfare is ultimately governed by sustainability. Missile stockpiles, industrial production capacity, domestic political legitimacy and alliance commitments become as decisive as battlefield success. General Yakovleff contends that the United States retains ample military capability to continue operations against Iran in isolation, yet doing so progressively erodes its ability to deter other adversaries, reassure allies and sustain global commitments.
events.ticker_label: 🪖 'Trump Needs a Way Out of This War': General Yakovlev explains 'charade' over US-Iran negotiations

events.title: New Victorian premier Ben Carroll says ‘I will do things differently’ – as it happened
events.description: This blog is now closed Jacinta Allan resigns as Victorian premier before leadership challenge by Ben Carroll Who is Ben Carroll? We thought about this and we just think that it’s time for renewal. The union movement is in good shape. We’ve seen changes in workers’ rights that have made a big difference in workers’ lives. We’ve seen the union movement starting to grow for the first time in decades. And next year will be the 100th anniversary of the ACTU. So we think it’s time for a new leadership team to come in. We have a debt heading towards $200bn in this state. We have teachers out striking in the streets because the state government and Ben Carroll can’t secure a pay deal. We have holes in the roads. You need a majority government to fix those problems, and you need someone with a plan. Now he might performatively call a royal commission tokenistically, now that he’s become leader, but that’s not out of sincere concern about corruption.
